html:
The Koh-i-Noor is a large diamond of India, now set in the British crown jewels. Its name is Persian for "mountain of light". Its early history is hazy.

By the 1600s it was held by the Mughal emperors and set in the Peacock Throne of Shah Jahan. After Nader Shah of Persia sacked Delhi in 1739, he took it, along with the throne. After his murder it passed to the Afghan Durrani rulers, and then to Ranjit Singh, the ruler of the Sikh Empire.

When the British annexed the Punjab in 1849, the treaty ended with the diamond handed to Queen Victoria. It was shown at the Great Exhibition of 1851, and then recut. It has since been worn by queens, not kings. India and other states have asked for its return; the British government has refused.
